name: NEET (UG) for MBBS: Class 12 marks in PCB
note: The NMC regulations confirm the subjects (Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Biotechnology, and English) but give no percentage. The 50 / 40 / 45 figures here are the DCI rule for BDS, used as a guide: the NEET bulletin could not be read. Confirm in the NEET (UG) information bulletin.

name: BDS: Class 12 marks in PCB
confidence: official page (DCI regulations, 2007 text as amended)
note: The third figure (45%) is for a lower-limb locomotory disability, not every benchmark disability. Confirm in the current NEET bulletin and DCI notices.

name: BVSc & AH, 15% all-India quota (via NEET)
note: Aggregate of English, Physics, Chemistry and Biology: 50%, and 47.5% for SC/ST and other special categories. No separate figure for the third category was found, so the General figure is used.

name: B.Sc Nursing: PCB and English
confidence: official page (INC), with one part not confirmed
note: The INC page says 45% aggregate and states no category relaxation. A draft 2022 INC corrigendum gives 40% for SC/ST/OBC but is not confirmed in force, so the reserved category shows Check between 40% and 45%. The admission route is set by your state or university.

name: B.Sc Agriculture (ICAR, via CUET UG 2026)
note: Counted over all Class 12 subjects, not PCB only; at least three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture. 50% General, OBC-NCL and EWS; 40% SC, ST and PwBD. Universities add their own conditions.

name: MBBS/BDS state quota, Maharashtra (State CET Cell, via NEET)
note: From the official 2025-26 NEET brochure of the State CET Cell (PCB aggregate: Open and EWS 50%, reserved categories and SEBC 40%, General-category PwD 45%); the 2026-27 brochure could not be retrieved. Domicile of Maharashtra and Maharashtra schooling are required, with listed exceptions.

name: B.Tech niche disciplines, Maharashtra (MHT-CET PCB group)
note: Physics and Chemistry compulsory plus Mathematics or Biology; limited to nine disciplines; a non-zero MHT-CET PCB score is needed. Open 45%, EWS and reserved 40%.

name: Agriculture and allied degrees, Maharashtra (MHT-CET, NEET or JEE)
note: Class 12 Science aggregate: 45% General, 40% reserved including EWS and physically handicapped candidates. The brochure still carries some 2025 wording.

name: MBBS/BDS state quota, Kerala (CEE, via NEET)
note: Aggregate of Physics, Chemistry and Biology, with English passed separately; 40% for SC/ST/SEBC and PwD; plus the NEET (UG) 50th percentile (40th for SC/ST/SEBC; PwD 45th unreserved).

name: Agriculture, forestry and fisheries, Kerala (KAU, via NEET)
note: General 50% in PCB; SEBC and PwD 45%; SC/ST need only the pass mark (shown as 0 to 45). NEET (UG) minimum 20 marks, SC/ST exempt.

name: BVSc & AH, Kerala (via NEET)
note: Aggregate of English, Physics, Chemistry and Biology; 47.5% for SC/ST/SEBC/PwD.

name: AP EAPCET (Andhra Pradesh): B.Pharm, agriculture, biotech (BiPC)
note: 45% General and 40% reserved in the subjects specified (B.Pharm needs Biology, Physics and Chemistry). No PwD figure in the booklet text, so the General figure is used. Rank: 75% EAPCET and 25% Intermediate marks.

name: GGSIPU (Delhi): MBBS
note: 50% aggregate in PCB (40% SC/ST), English passed, and NEET (UG) qualification. OBC and PwD figures were not stated on the page read, so the General figure is used for the third category. Age 17 by 31 December; NEET merit decides.

name: GGSIPU (Delhi): B.Sc (Hons) Nursing
note: 45% in PCB taken together, English passed; unmarried female candidates only; NEET (UG) 2026 merit first, then the university CET. Reserved-category relaxation is not stated, so the General figure is used.

name: GGSIPU (Delhi): BPT / BOT
note: 50% aggregate in PCB, each subject passed, English passed; NEET (UG) 2026 merit. Reserved relaxation is not stated, so the General figure is used.

name: Kerala MBBS/BDS: NRI quota and OCI/PIO (KEAM 2026)
note: NEET (UG) qualification and 50% in PCB together (40% for SC/ST/SEBC/PwD), with English passed. No separate NRI figure: this is Kerala all-category rule. A candidate dependent on a close relative working abroad can use the NRI quota with sponsor documents. OCI/PIO are treated at par with Indian citizens for admission only, with no reservation or fee concession.
